A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same VB/StA research, with matching methods and benchmark tables. All supplied pages were inspected. Neither PDF contains an appendix or attached supplement, despite references to supplementary material.

before.justification: V1 reports original cross-dataset and cross-manipulation detection results, component ablations and corruption-robustness evaluations in Tables 1–6 and Figure 4.

after.justification: V2 retains the original detection results and adds a fusion ablation and qualitative adapter/blending analyses in Table 9 and Figures 4–5.

M1.justification: The VB synthesis procedure and StA architecture remain unchanged, including landmark perturbation, regional blending, spatial/temporal convolutions and cross-attention. The new fusion comparison evaluates an ablation rather than revising the proposed method.

E1.justification: FF++ training, seven cross-dataset benchmarks and eight DF40 manipulation types are retained. V2 omits the Gaussian-blur, blockwise-distortion, contrast and JPEG-corruption scenarios reported in v1, while adding a repeated-frame versus normal-video diagnostic.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the six retained result tables is unchanged. V2 adds evaluated CBI and PFIG synthesis comparisons and a linear-fusion control, while omitting v1's multi-detector robustness comparison, which included FWA, Face X-ray and PatchForensics.

E3.justification: FF++ c23 training, CLIP ViT-l14, 32 sampled frames, eight-frame clips and AUC/Acc/EER metrics remain unchanged. V2 adds fusion-control and repeated-image GradCAM procedures; v1's five-severity-level corruption protocol is absent.

E4.justification: The supporting analyses are substantially revised. V1's robustness study is omitted, while v2 adds cross-attention versus linear-fusion ablation (Table 9), adapter activation diagnostics (Figure 4), and comparisons of how VB, CBI and PFIG reproduce FFD (Figure 5). The original backbone, VB/StA and SBI/VB ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations or statistical significance tests. The added results retain point-estimate and qualitative reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in v1 Tables 1–6 match v2 Tables 3–8. V2 adds supplementary fusion results, including CDF-v2 AUC 0.886 for linear combination versus 0.947 for cross-attention, and qualitative adapter/synthesis findings. V1's corruption-response curves are omitted.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Equations 1–6 retain the same mathematical content. V2's notation table restates existing definitions; no new theoretical assumptions, derivations or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the main claims: identifying FFD, simulating it through VB, and efficiently learning spatial and temporal forgery cues with StA. The new analyses support these existing claims.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the fusion ablation as evidence of high-level spatial/temporal complementarity and explains why CBI and PFIG inadequately mimic FFD. It also removes v1's explicit footnote excluding whole-image synthesis from the paper's scope.

D1.justification: V2 removes v1's code/pretrained-weights URL without replacement. It also changes the stated provenance of baseline scores from benchmark reproduction to cited sources (Table 3) and identifies official pretrained-model evaluation for AltFreezing (Table 4). These disclosures do not establish that experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: V2 adds a synthesis-method comparison table and references including OST, PCL and the PFIG source. It removes brief coverage of parameter-efficient, training-free, landmark-based and debiasing approaches and adds localization/attention-based work. The central video-blending motivation remains.

P1.justification: V2 consolidates the three generalization subsections, rewrites the dataset/protocol description and removes the duplicated Protocol-3 discussion. It also updates author/affiliation text, adopts numbered citations and edits related-work and conclusion wording. Most introduction and method prose is retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds substantial new displays: the comparison and notation tables, fusion-ablation table, and two diagnostic figures. V1's robustness figure is omitted. Existing result tables are renumbered and repositioned, and typography, captions and page layout are reformatted throughout.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens architectural justification through Table 9 and Figures 4–5 and clarifies baseline-result provenance. However, it removes the corruption-robustness evidence and code/weight-access disclosure. These material gains and losses affect different aspects of evidential strength and reproducibility, leaving the net quality direction uncertain; the main benchmark results are unchanged.
